paras_en: On August 2, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – U.S. equities will face two major tests this week. On one hand, more than a quarter of S&P 500 companies are set to release earnings; on the other, the July non‑farm payrolls report due on August 7 could sway market expectations about a possible Fed rate hike in September.

The market’s biggest focus is no longer just AI company earnings but whether the economy remains overheated. If the labor market stays strong, it suggests inflationary pressure may be hard to cool, increasing the likelihood of further Fed tightening.

Current forecasts put July’s U.S. non‑farm payroll increase at 83,000 jobs with the unemployment rate holding at 4.3%. A higher‑than‑expected jobs gain could prompt the market to bet again on a September rate hike. Rate‑futures now imply about a 64% probability of a September increase.

The Fed left rates unchanged last week, but new chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the goal of bringing inflation down to 2%. He did not spell out the next policy step, leaving the market more dependent on economic data to gauge the rate path.

Beyond the data, this week is also a key earnings week in the U.S. season, with companies such as Eli Lilly (LLY‑US), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD‑US), Palantir Technologies (PLTR‑US), Caterpillar (CAT‑US) and Merck (MRK‑US) slated to report Q2 results.

AI‑related stocks remain in the spotlight, but recent performance is diverging. Microsoft (MSFT‑US) saw its stock post the biggest single‑day gain since 2008 on optimism about cloud growth, while Meta Platforms (META‑US) suffered a sharp drop after a steep cash‑flow decline, reflecting investors’ growing emphasis on profit quality over pure AI hype.

In addition, Elon Musk’s SpaceX will release its first quarterly report since going public this week, and the market will watch to see whether its performance further influences investor risk appetite.

items.title: 本週操盤筆記：美7月非農、SpaceX超微Sandisk財報、AI行情及中東局勢
items.title_en: This Week's Trading Notes: US July Nonfarm Payrolls, SpaceX, AMD, SanDisk Earnings, AI Market and Middle East Tensions
paras: 本週國際大事包括美國 7 月非農就業報告，還有一系列企業財報，包括 SpaceX(SPCX-US)將於週二公布首次公開發行 (IPO) 後第一份季報，以及晶片製造商超微、記憶體股 Sandisk(SNDK-US)和大型製藥商禮來 (Eli Lilly)(LLY-US) 等。

1、就業報告成 Fed 會後首場大考

市場將於本週五迎接美國 7 月非農就業報告，路透訪調的經濟學家預估，7 月非農新增就業 9.1 萬人，失業率維持在 4.3%。
若就業數據優於預期，可能進一步提高市場對聯準會 (Fed)9 月升息的預期，以抑制持續高於目標的通膨。根據 LSEG 資料，截至上週五的聯邦基金利率期貨顯示，市場預估 Fed 9 月升息機率約 64%。
Fed 上週三維持利率不變，但有三位官員主張升息，主席華許 (Kevin Warsh) 也重申，Fed 將堅定致力於讓通膨回到 2% 目標。但是，投資人仍不清楚華許打算透過何種方式達成這項長期目標。
考量到華許主張減少 Fed 對未來政策的前瞻指引 (forward guidance)，市場未來將更加聚焦經濟數據，這自然也包括本週五的就業報告。
Plante Moran Financial Advisors 投資長 Jim Baird 表示，新任 Fed 領導層在前瞻指引、透明度與溝通方式上的思維已有重大改變，「因此，市場對重要經濟數據公布時的反應，未來可能會更加劇烈，因為市場對政策方向的掌握變得沒那麼清楚。」

2、市場緊盯重量級財報

本週將有逾四分之一標普 500 企業公布財報，包括製藥商禮來 (LLY-US)、晶片設計商超微(AMD-US)、開拓重工(Caterpillar)(CAT-US)、Palantir Technologies(PLTR-US) 及 Merck(MRK-US)。
最受矚目的可能還是 SpaceX 將於週二公布 6 月 IPO 後首份季報，執行長馬斯克預定參與，投資人最關注星鏈 (Starlink) 的成長、星艦 (Starship ) 開發時程及資本支出規畫。
SpaceX 股價在上市一度大漲，但之後一路走弱，因此這份財報可能影響整體市場風險偏好。
根據 LSEG IBES 資料，在已公布及市場預估結果計算下，標普 500 企業第 2 季調整後 EPS 預估年增 29.3%。

3、AI 行情劇烈震盪

SK 海力士 (SKHY-US) 的 IPO 緘默期將結束，屆時分析師可開始正式發布對這家記憶體巨擘的投資建議評等。
SK 海力士上週五在首爾交易的股價飆升 30%，收在每股 171.8 萬韓元 (約 1197 美元)，觸及南韓股市單日漲跌幅限制。相較之下，其美國存託憑證 (ADR) 當天收盤卻下跌 3.6%，報每股 143.69 美元，仍低於 7 月 9 日的 IPO 發行價 149 美元。
AI 行情正進入劇烈震盪的時期，投資人正在擔憂 AI 獲利能力、競爭加劇，以及龐大資本支出究竟由誰買單。最典型的案例就是南韓 Kospi 指數，該指數在過去六週暴跌 40% 後，上週五又在 SK 海力士和三星電子強漲拉抬下，暴漲 18%。

4、中東戰事持續升溫

市場仍將密切關注中東局勢。美國與伊朗 6 月中旬宣布的停火協議，如今看來已成過眼雲煙，油價再度逼近每桶 90 美元。
這場持續五個月的衝突可能開闢新戰線，因為近日埃及地中海港口達米埃塔 (Damietta) 兩艘美國天然氣運輸船遭無人機攻擊，這讓人擔憂，全球重要航運要道蘇伊士運河恐面臨威脅。
此外，沙烏地阿拉伯本週首度公開與美軍聯手空襲伊朗支持的伊拉克東部武裝組織，同時，美軍對伊朗發動所稱的「大規模」空襲，以回應伊朗企圖對美軍基地發射彈道飛彈。
在此同時，外交斡旋行動仍在持續，沙國正推動 14 國聯盟，加強曼德海峽 (Bab el-Mandeb)、紅海與亞丁灣等全球能源運輸要道的海上防衛。
paras_en: This week’s international headlines include the US July nonfarm payroll report and a series of corporate earnings, such as SpaceX (SPCX-US) which will release its first quarterly report after its IPO on Tuesday, chipmaker AMD, memory‑chip stock SanDisk (SNDK-US) and large‑pharma company Eli Lilly (LLY-US).
This week’s trading notes (20260803‑0808)

1. The jobs report is the Fed’s first big test after the meeting
The market will await the US July nonfarm payrolls on Friday. Reuters‑surveyed economists forecast 91,000 new jobs in July and an unemployment rate holding at 4.3%. If the data beat expectations, it could raise market expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike rates again in September to curb inflation that remains above target. LSEG data show that, as of last Friday, Fed‑funds futures priced a roughly 64% probability of a September rate hike.
The Fed left rates unchanged on Wednesday, but three officials advocated a hike, and Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the Fed’s commitment to bring inflation back to its 2% goal. However, investors remain unclear on how Warsh plans to achieve that long‑term target.
Because Warsh favors less forward guidance from the Fed, the market will focus even more on economic data, including Friday’s jobs report.
Jim Baird, CIO of Plante Moran Financial Advisors, said the new Fed leadership has markedly changed its thinking on forward guidance, transparency and communication, “so market reactions to key economic releases may become more extreme, as the view of policy direction becomes less clear.”

2. Markets are glued to heavyweight earnings
More than a quarter of S&P 500 constituents will report earnings this week, including pharma giant Eli Lilly (LLY‑US), chip designer AMD (AMD‑US), Caterpillar (CAT‑US), Palantir Technologies (PLTR‑US) and Merck (MRK‑US).
The most watched may be SpaceX, which will release its first post‑IPO June quarter on Tuesday. CEO Elon Musk is expected to attend, and investors will focus on Starlink growth, Starship development timelines and capital‑expenditure plans.
SpaceX’s stock surged after the listing but has since weakened, so this filing could affect overall market risk appetite.
According to LSEG IBES, the consensus adjusted Q2 EPS for S&P 500 companies is up 29.3% year‑over‑year based on reported and estimated results.
3. AI market swings wildly
SK Hynix’s (SKHY‑US) IPO lock‑up period ends, allowing analysts to publish formal investment‑rating recommendations.
SK Hynix shares jumped 30% on the Seoul exchange last Friday, closing at 1.718 million KRW (about $1,197) and hitting the daily price‑limit. By contrast, its ADR fell 3.6% that day, closing at $143.69, still below the July 9 IPO price of $149.
The AI sector is entering a period of sharp volatility as investors worry about AI profitability, intensifying competition and who will foot massive cap‑ex bills. The most vivid example is South Korea’s KOSPI, which after a 40% slide over six weeks, surged 18% last Friday on strong gains in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.
4. Middle‑East conflict continues to heat up
Markets will keep a close eye on the Middle East. The cease‑fire announced by the US and Iran in mid‑June now appears to have evaporated, and oil prices are again approaching $90 a barrel.
The five‑month‑long war could open a new front after two US LNG carriers were hit by drone attacks at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta, raising concerns that the vital Suez Canal could be threatened.
Saudi Arabia also disclosed for the first time this week that it coordinated air strikes with US forces against Iran‑backed militias in eastern Iraq, while the US launched what it called a “large‑scale” air campaign against Iran in response to Tehran’s attempt to fire a ballistic missile at a US base.
Meanwhile diplomatic efforts continue, with Saudi Arabia pushing a 14‑nation coalition to bolster maritime security in the Bab el‑Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, key global energy‑transport routes.

items.title: 國防股跌出機會？「這家公司」估值回落、分析師看漲32%
items.title_en: Defense Stocks Miss Opportunity? Valuation of "This Company" Falls, Analysts Bullish 32%
paras: 儘管中東戰事未歇、全球地緣政治風險持續升溫，加上財報表現亮眼，國防類股理應迎來多頭行情，但美股國防相關個股近期表現卻普遍疲軟，與基本面走勢背道而馳。不過分析師指出，在這波修正後，部分大型軍工股評價已跌至具吸引力的水準，其中又以 L3 哈里斯科技 (LHX-US) 最受華爾街青睞。
根據《巴隆周刊》報導，L3 哈里斯週三（29 日）公布第二季財報後，股價次日重挫近 9%，單看股價反應，外界或許以為財報表現不佳，但事實恰恰相反。
實際上，若不計一次性項目，L3 哈里斯每股盈餘較去年同期成長 28%，優於華爾街預期，公司同時還上調了全年財務展望。
唯一公布的一項負面消息，是公司宣布將旗下飛彈相關業務的首次公開募股（IPO）計畫延期，理由是「市場環境」所致。
分析指出，所謂的「市場環境」，很可能指的是國防科技類股估值倍數大幅下滑。目前 L3 哈里斯股價約為未來 12 個月預估每股盈餘的 20 倍本益比，低於伊朗衝突爆發時約 30 倍的水準。
報導稱，伊朗戰事對國防類股造成的影響頗為弔詭。儘管飛彈與無人機需求暢旺、業務蓬勃發展，相關個股股價卻反向走跌。
之所以會造成此情況似乎是因為市場憂心，一旦這場民意支持度不高的戰爭告一段落，國防支出成長動能恐將趨緩。
然而，目前尚未看到支出放緩的跡象。事實上，無人機與飛彈相關支出仍持續攀升，讓大型國防股的估值顯得格外值得關注。
根據 FactSet 資料，分析師對 L3 哈里斯的平均目標價約為 366 美元，較一年前的 302 美元明顯上調；以目前約 277.06 美元的股價計算，仍有約 32% 的潛在上漲空間。
這使 L3 哈里斯目前成為美國大型國防承包商中，股價與分析師目標價落差最大的一家公司，其他同業還包括諾斯洛普格拉曼 (NOC-US) 、洛克希德馬丁 (LMT-US) 、通用動力 (GD-US) 及 Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII-US) 。
過去一年，上述國防股的分析師平均目標價上調了 23%，但股價同期僅平均上漲 13%。其中，L3 哈里斯與諾斯洛普格拉曼過去 12 個月仍呈下跌。
因此，依據分析師目標價推算的平均潛在漲幅，已由一年前約 7% 擴大至目前約 17%。
此外，L3 哈里斯也是分析師最看好的國防股，71% 的分析師給予「買進」評等。相較之下，標普 500 成分股的平均買進評等比例約為 55% 至 60%，其他大型國防承包商的平均買進評等則約為 56%。
分析指出，儘管分析師觀點會隨時間調整，目標價亦僅是評估投資機會的其中一項指標。但就目前華爾街的看法而言，L3 哈里斯無疑是這波國防股修正中最受青睞的標的，只是市場投資人似乎尚未買單。
另外，市值較小、專注於自主系統與無人機技術的 Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (KTOS-US) 也值得注意。
其分析師平均目標價已從一年前約 57 美元上調至 106 美元，但股價過去一年反而下跌 21%，目前仍比平均目標價低約 57%，代表若達到目標價，潛在漲幅高達 130%。
Kratos 在伊朗衝突爆發前，本益比一度超過 160 倍；如今已降至 50 倍以下，再次凸顯近期國防產業股票估值波動之劇烈。
paras_en: Despite ongoing Middle East conflicts, rising global geopolitical risks, and strong earnings reports that should fuel a bullish trend for defense stocks, U.S. defense equities have recently been broadly weak, diverging from fundamentals. Analysts note that after this correction, valuations of several large defense firms have slipped to attractive levels, with L3Harris Technologies (LHX-US) being the most favored on Wall Street.

According to Barron's, L3Harris saw its stock plunge nearly 9% the day after it released its Q2 earnings on Wednesday (the 29th). At first glance the price drop might suggest a disappointing report, but the reality is the opposite.
In fact, excluding one‑time items, L3Harris earnings per share grew 28% year‑over‑year, beating Wall Street expectations, and the company also raised its full‑year outlook.
The only negative news disclosed was the postponement of the initial public offering for its missile‑related business, attributed to "market conditions."

Analysts point out that "market conditions" likely refer to the sharp decline in valuation multiples for defense‑technology stocks. L3Harris now trades at about 20 times forward 12‑month earnings, down from roughly 30 times during the height of the Iran conflict.
The report says the impact of the Iran war on defense stocks has been paradoxical: despite strong demand for missiles and drones and robust business growth, related share prices have fallen.
This appears to stem from market concerns that once this low‑public‑support war ends, the momentum in defense‑spending growth could slow.
However, no slowdown in spending has yet materialized. Drone and missile expenditures continue to rise, keeping valuations of large defense stocks under close watch.
FactSet data show analysts’ average target price for L3Harris at $366, up from $302 a year ago; at the current price of about $277.06, this implies roughly 32% upside potential.

This makes L3Harris the U.S. large‑cap defense contractor with the widest gap between its share price and analysts’ targets, ahead of peers such as Northrop Grumman (NOC-US), Lockheed Martin (LMT-US), General Dynamics (GD-US) and Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII-US).

Over the past year, analysts raised average target prices for the above defense stocks by 23%, while their share prices rose only 13% on average. L3Harris and Northrop Grumman have actually declined over the last 12 months.
Thus, the average potential upside based on analysts’ targets has expanded from about 7% a year ago to roughly 17% today.

Moreover, L3Harris is the most favored defense stock among analysts, with 71% assigning a "Buy" rating. By comparison, the S&P 500 average buy rating sits around 55%–60%, and other large defense contractors average about 56% buy ratings.

Analysts note that while views can change over time and target prices are just one metric, Wall Street currently sees L3Harris as the most attractive pick in the defense‑stock correction, even though investors have yet to act on it.
Another smaller‑cap player focused on autonomous systems and drone technology, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (KTOS-US), also merits attention.

Its analysts’ average target price has risen from about $57 a year ago to $106, yet the stock has fallen 21% over the past year and still trades roughly 57% below the average target, implying a potential upside of up to 130% if the target is met.
Before the Iran conflict erupted, Kratos traded at a price‑to‑earnings multiple exceeding 160×; it has now fallen below 50×, underscoring the dramatic valuation swings in the defense sector recently.

items.title: 美財長貝森特手寫紙條曝光！美國罕見出手救日元  背後是美債危機考量？
items.title_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent’s Handwritten Note Exposed! Rare U.S. Intervention to Support the Yen – Driven by Concerns Over a U.S. Debt Crisis?
paras: 日元兌美元上週四（30 日）、五（31 日）連續劇烈震盪，一度觸及 1986 年以來最低水準，市場原本已預期日本政府將再度進場干預匯市。然而真正引發全球關注的，卻是華府這回竟也罕見出手相挺。
多家外媒引述知情人士報導，美國政府週五指示紐約聯邦準備銀行執行「拋歐元、買日元」操作，協助穩住搖搖欲墜的日元匯價。
這項消息的最直接佐證，來自美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）一張被媒體鏡頭捕捉到的手寫紙條。
當地時間週五，川普在馬里蘭州戴維營度假地主持內閣會議並進行現場直播，貝森特一如往常坐在川普對面。
在鏡頭環伺之下，貝森特毫不避諱地在筆記本上寫下:「待辦事項：買進日元，50 億至 100 億美元。」這張紙條隨即被拍下並迅速在全球流傳開來。

三十年來罕見合作，分析憂心殃及美債

回顧過去三十年，美日兩國聯手干預匯市的紀錄僅有兩次：

一次是 1998 年亞洲金融風暴期間，雙方協同買進日元；
另一次則發生在 2011 年東日本大地震後，日元一度異常飆升，美國與其他七國隨即與日本展開聯合干預行動。


值得玩味的是，貝森特過去正是外匯市場的老手，曾在 2012 年主導索羅斯基金放空日元，短短三個月內大賺逾十億美元。
如今卻反過來親自下場「馳援」日元，外界解讀此舉恐怕別有考量，即避免日本金融情勢失控，進而波及美國公債市場。
畢竟受美伊軍事緊張及聯準會新任主席華許（Kevin Warsh）信任危機影響，美國長天期公債殖利率上週才剛創下次貸風暴以來新高。
事實上，今年 1 月日本首相高市早苗財政政策一度引爆「日債風暴」，花旗集團當時便警告，該波動盪恐觸發規模高達 1300 億美元的美債拋售潮。
據悉，美方官員私下已向日方表達憂慮，擔心高市早苗的激進財政路線可能重演英國前首相特拉斯（Liz Truss）當年引爆市場崩跌的覆轍。

日本外匯存底加速消耗，成效仍待觀察

儘管日本當局近期已大手筆動用外匯存底救市，成效卻相當有限。
市場估算，光是上週四單日，日本政府與央行的干預規模就達到 6 兆至 7 兆日元，加上 4 月底至 5 月底期間投入的 11.7 兆日元（約合 743 億美元），累計干預金額已攀升至 18 兆日元（約 1143 億美元），一舉超越 2024 年創下的 15.3 兆日元歷史紀錄。
美國財政部先前公布的國際資本流動報告也顯示，日本 5 月確實拋售了 667.5 億美元美國公債，金額與其外匯干預規模大致吻合。
然而，那波干預效果僅維持約一個月，日元至 6 月初便已貶回干預前的低點。
日本財務省週六凌晨也透過社群媒體發文表示，在適當情況下不排除動用聯準會的「外國暨國際貨幣當局常設回購機制」(FIMA Repo Facility)，透過以美國公債作為擔保品，取得臨時性美元流動性支援。
外界解讀，貝森特似乎也意識到，單靠匯市砸錢恐怕無法根治日元貶值問題。他週五特別在社群平台上發文，表示期待 8 月底於 G20 會議期間與日本央行總裁植田和男「再度會面」。
巧合的是，植田和男上週五在宣布維持利率不變後，亦於會後記者會上罕見鬆口，暗示未來不排除「加快升息步伐」的可能性。
paras_en: The yen versus the dollar saw violent swings on Thursday (the 30th) and Friday (the 31st) last week, briefly hitting its lowest level since 1986. Markets had expected the Japanese government to step in again to intervene in the FX market. However, the story that captured global attention was that Washington this time also made a rare move to support the currency.

Several foreign media outlets, citing insiders, reported that the U.S. government instructed the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Friday to carry out a “sell euros, buy yen” operation to help steady the wobbling yen exchange rate.
The most direct evidence of this came from a handwritten note by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that was captured on camera by the media.

On Friday local time, President Trump hosted a cabinet meeting and live broadcast from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Maryland, with Bessent seated opposite him as usual. Under the watchful eye of the cameras, Bessent unabashedly wrote in his notebook: “To‑do: buy yen, $5‑10 billion.” The note was immediately photographed and quickly spread worldwide.
A collaboration not seen in thirty years raises worries about U.S. debt

Looking back over the past three decades, there have been only two instances of joint U.S.–Japan intervention in the FX market: one during the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when both sides coordinated to buy yen; and another after the 2011 Great East Japan earthquake, when the yen surged sharply and the U.S. and seven other countries joined Japan in a coordinated intervention.

It is noteworthy that Bessent himself was once a veteran of the FX market, having led a Soros fund short‑sell of the yen in 2012, netting more than $1 billion in profit within three months. Now he is personally “rushing to the rescue” of the yen, which analysts interpret as a move motivated by concerns that a loss of control over Japan’s financial situation could spill over into the U.S. Treasury market.

Indeed, amid heightened U.S.–Iran tensions and a credibility crisis for new Fed chair Kevin Warsh, long‑term U.S. Treasury yields only last week reached their highest level since the last debt‑crisis‑induced credit crunch.

In fact, in January this year Japanese Prime Minister Naïve Takashi’s fiscal policy sparked a “Japanese‑bond storm,” prompting Citigroup to warn that the turbulence could trigger up to $130 billion of U.S. Treasury sell‑offs.
U.S. officials have reportedly privately expressed concern to Japan that Takashi’s aggressive fiscal stance could repeat the market collapse caused by former UK Prime Minister Liz Truss.
Japan’s foreign‑exchange reserves are being depleted rapidly, and the impact of recent interventions remains uncertain
Although Japanese authorities have recently deployed massive foreign‑exchange reserves to prop up the market, the effect has been limited.

Market estimates put last Thursday’s single‑day intervention by the Japanese government and central bank at ¥6‑7 trillion, and combined with the ¥11.7 trillion (about $74.3 billion) deployed from the end of April to the end of May, total intervention has risen to ¥18 trillion (about $114.3 billion), surpassing the record ¥15.3 trillion set in 2024.
The U.S. Treasury’s International Capital Flows report also shows that Japan sold $66.75 billion of U.S. Treasuries in May, an amount roughly matching the scale of its FX intervention.
However, that wave of intervention only lasted about a month; by early June the yen had already slipped back to its pre‑intervention lows.

In the early hours of Saturday, Japan’s Ministry of Finance posted on social media that, if appropriate, it would not rule out using the Federal Reserve’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Permanent Repo Facility (FIMA Repo) to obtain temporary dollar liquidity by pledging U.S. Treasuries as collateral.

Observers note that Bessent seems to realize that simply throwing money at the FX market cannot cure the yen’s depreciation. On Friday he posted on social media that he looks forward to meeting Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda again at the G20 summit at the end of August.

Coincidentally, after announcing that rates would remain unchanged last Friday, Ueda also made a rare comment at the post‑meeting press conference, hinting that a faster pace of rate hikes could not be ruled out in the future.

items.title: 參考港靈活槓桿框架！韓擬修法賦監管「緊急降槓桿權」 2倍ETF遇險可瞬降至1倍
items.title_en: Referencing Hong Kong's Flexible Leverage Framework! South Korea Plans to Amend Law Granting Regulators "Emergency Leverage Reduction Power"; 2x ETFs Could Instantly Drop to 1x
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，南韓金融委員會 (FSC) 與金融監督院 (FSS) 正共同起草《金融投資業與資本市場法》修正案，打算首度引入「緊急行動權限」，賦予監管機關在市場劇烈波動時可繞過受益人大會表決，直接把單一股票槓桿 ETF 的追蹤倍數由現行 2 倍臨時調降至 1.5 倍或 1 倍，為危機時刻快速拆彈提供法源。
《韓聯社》報導，此舉直指今夏韓股「七月風暴」禍源。南韓 5 月放行追蹤三星電子、SK 海力士單日表現的 2 倍個股槓桿 ETF 後，散戶湧入、機械再平衡賣壓在下跌中放大波動，KOSPI 與 KOSDAQ 上月底接連觸發熔斷，副總理具潤哲公開致歉，坦承制度引入時未充分評估風險。
除緊急降倍數外，監管層同步研議三道閘門：設個人槓桿投資額度上限 (傳擬限總投資部位 20%)、把基本保證金門檻從 1000 萬韓元提至 3000 萬韓元、對大額交易者強制模擬交易義務。
南韓修法思路從「事後喊話」轉向「事前預防＋緊急干預」，並參考香港證監會 7 月 24 日靈活槓桿框架，允許極端市況下把做多產品目標槓桿降至 1.1 倍。
FSC 委員長李億遠在國會表示，下調倍數對緩解波動「預計有效」，但修法須兼顧受益人權益與緊急響應速度。
業內人士解讀，若修正案闖關成功，南韓將成為繼香港後，亞洲第二個把「槓桿倍數」納入監管即時調節工具箱的市場，未來散戶再想靠單股 2 倍 ETF 來博晶片反彈，將碰上監管按下減速鍵，槓桿紅利可能被瞬間腰斬。
paras_en: Foreign media reports say South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) are jointly drafting an amendment to the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act that would introduce, for the first time, an “emergency action authority.” This would allow regulators, during periods of extreme market volatility, to bypass beneficiary voting and directly lower the tracking multiple of a single‑stock leveraged ETF from the current 2‑times to a temporary 1.5‑times or 1‑times, providing a legal basis for rapid “defusing” in a crisis.

The Yonhap News Agency says the move is aimed squarely at the source of this summer’s Korean‑stock “July storm.” After South Korea opened 2‑times single‑stock leveraged ETFs that track Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix in May, retail investors poured in and mechanical rebalancing sell pressure amplified price swings on the decline. The KOSPI and KOSDAQ both hit circuit‑breakers at the end of the month, prompting Deputy Prime Minister Heo Roon‑cheol to publicly apologize and admit that the system was introduced without sufficient risk assessment.

In addition to the emergency leverage‑reduction tool, regulators are also studying three “gates”: setting a cap on individual leveraged‑investment exposure (proposed at a maximum of 20% of total investment positions), raising the basic margin requirement from 10 million won to 30 million won, and imposing a mandatory simulated‑trading obligation on large‑volume traders.

South Korea’s legislative approach is shifting from “post‑event commentary” to “pre‑emptive prevention plus emergency intervention,” and it draws on the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission’s flexible‑leverage framework announced on July 24, which allows the target leverage of long‑only products to be cut to 1.1‑times under extreme market conditions.

FSC Chairman Lee Ik‑won told parliament that lowering the multiple is expected to be effective in easing volatility, but any amendment must balance beneficiary rights with the speed of emergency response.

Industry insiders interpret that if the amendment passes, South Korea will become, after Hong Kong, the second Asian market to place “leverage multiples” into a real‑time regulatory adjustment toolbox. In the future, retail investors hoping to chase a chip‑sector rebound with single‑stock 2‑times ETFs will face a regulatory “slow‑down button,” and the leverage premium could be slashed in an instant.

items.title: Google Earth AI生圖緊急喊卡 虛構場景可疊加衛星圖散播假消息
items.title_en: Google Earth AI Image Generation Halted Over Misinformation Risks
paras: Google 推出 Google Earth 人工智慧（AI）圖像生成功能不到 48 小時宣布暫停服務，以加強安全防護。專家警告，這項工具可把虛構場景疊加在真實衛星圖像上，容易被用於散播假消息。
據英國《BBC》報導，這項新功能把 Google 圖像生成器 Nano Banana 2 整合進 Google Earth。用戶只須輸入文字指令，就能在真實衛星圖像、航拍圖像或三維地圖上生成虛構場景，下載後分享到其他平台。
《BBC》核查團隊測試時，成功生成埃菲爾鐵塔倒塌、巨大天坑吞沒埃及金字塔，以及俄軍坦克出現在基輔等假圖像。
專家指出，虛構內容與真實地理坐標和 Google Earth 底圖結合後，容易讓人誤以為圖像來自可靠衛星資料。在戰爭、災害等消息混亂時期，這類圖像尤其可能誤導記者和民眾。
Google 說，AI 生成圖像含隱形水印，用戶可通過 Gemini 或 Google Lens 核查。不過，《BBC》測試發現，部分驗證機制可被繞過，外部檢測工具有時也無法識別假圖。
paras_en: Google announced a pause to its new AI image generation feature in Google Earth less than 48 hours after launch, citing the need to strengthen safety safeguards. Experts warned that the tool can overlay fabricated scenes onto real satellite imagery, making it easy to spread false information.

According to the BBC, the feature integrates Google’s image generator Nano Banana 2 into Google Earth. Users simply enter a text prompt and the system creates fictional scenes on top of real satellite photos, aerial shots, or 3‑D maps, which can then be downloaded and shared on other platforms.

In the BBC’s verification tests, the tool successfully produced fake images such as the Eiffel Tower collapsed, a massive sinkhole swallowing the Egyptian pyramids, and Russian tanks appearing in Kyiv.

Experts note that when fictional content is combined with authentic geographic coordinates and Google Earth’s base maps, viewers are likely to assume the images come from reliable satellite data. During chaotic periods such as wars or disasters, such images can especially mislead journalists and the public.

Google says AI‑generated images carry an invisible watermark that can be checked via Gemini or Google Lens. However, the BBC found that some verification mechanisms can be bypassed, and external detection tools sometimes fail to identify the fakes.

items.title: 日元空頭瑟瑟發抖！川普高調背書美日聯手託市、貝森特筆記泄露天機
items.title_en: Yen Short Sellers Tremble! Trump Boasts US‑Japan Joint Market Support, Bessent Note Leaks the Plan
paras: 美國總統川普證實，美國上週參與日本主導的外匯市場干預行動，協助支撐日元匯價，並形容此舉是對日本釋出的「友誼訊號」。他表示，美方支持盟友穩定金融市場，同時也預期能從相關安排中取得經濟利益。
川普週日（2 日）在搭乘空軍一號時向媒體表示，日本近期希望獲得美方協助，而美國一向支持日本，兩國維持良好關係。
他也提到，除了歷史上的珍珠港事件外，日本長期以來都是美國的重要夥伴，因此此次合作具有象徵雙邊友誼的意義。
對於美國參與干預能獲得哪些回報，川普僅表示將帶來「經濟利益」，並拿去年與阿根廷簽署的貨幣互換安排作為例子，稱儘管當時受到美國國內批評，但阿根廷今年已償還相關資金，美方最終「賺取了 250 億美元」。
美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）隨後也公開表態支持這項協同行動，強調近期日元出現過度且無序波動，美日因此共同採取外匯干預措施，以維護金融穩定。
他指出，美國財政部持續與日本財務省及日本銀行保持密切聯繫，必要時不排除再次聯手進場，並支持擴大聯準會的「外國與國際貨幣當局回購工具」，作為市場流動性的後盾。
日本財務省則表示，近期干預目的在於遏止日元異常波動，未來將持續與美國合作，必要時不排除進一步採取聯合行動，同時持續運用聯準會提供的流動性工具，並與美方保持密切溝通。

美日罕見聯手支撐日元 市場戒備後續干預

受美日協調干預及美元走弱影響，日元週一（3 日）亞洲盤初延續升勢，市場則密切觀察兩國是否將再次聯手進場。
此前，川普宣布暫緩對伊朗採取新的軍事行動，帶動美元回落，美元兌日元一度快速下跌約 100 點，跌至 156 附近，單日跌幅逾 1%。
日本與美國上週共同出手後，日元已明顯反彈。美元兌日元上週五收在 157.40 左右，創 5 月以來最佳表現；而在干預前，日元一度逼近 1986 年以來最低水準，美元兌日元曾接近 164。
市場人士指出，雖然全球每日外匯交易規模高達約 9.5 兆美元，官方干預未必足以扭轉日元長期走勢，但短線已成功逆轉日元連續數月的弱勢。
除了直接買入日元外，美日當局也透過要求銀行回報匯率報價，以及官員公開喊話等方式向市場施壓，提高放空日元的風險。
高盛分析師指出，若日元再度回吐近期漲幅，不排除官方未來數日再次進場干預，如同今年 5 月的情況。他們認為，在基本面尚未改善前，干預仍是官方爭取時間、穩定市場預期的有效工具。

日元疲弱牽動全球金融 美方憂衝擊美債市場

分析人士指出，日元近年持續承壓，主要受到能源價格上漲、日本財政赤字擴大，以及美日利差維持高檔等因素影響。
日元貶值雖有助日本出口競爭力，但也推升進口成本，增加企業與民眾負擔；另一方面，日本金融市場波動也可能透過全球資本流動影響其他市場，美國對此愈來愈關注。
瑞穗銀行策略師表示，這次事件的重要性不只在於干預本身，更代表市場開始相信，日元過度疲弱已不再只是日本的問題，而是可能牽動全球金融穩定。
市場也認為，美國支持日本干預還有另一層考量。若日本單獨支撐日元，可能需要出售更多美國公債換取美元資金，進一步推升美債殖利率並增加美國融資成本，因此美方選擇共同出手，有助降低日本大規模拋售美債的壓力。
外交關係委員會資深研究員 Rebecca Patterson 指出，日本已透過出售部分美債籌措干預資金，若未來出現更大規模資產配置調整，可能對美債市場帶來更大衝擊，因此說服日本避免持續出售美債，符合美國利益。
另一方面，《路透》日前公布的一張照片也引發市場關注。照片顯示，貝森特在戴維營內閣會議的筆記中，於待辦事項欄位寫下「買入 50 億至 100 億美元日元」，被視為美國積極參與干預的重要跡象。

日本央行按兵不動 市場仍關注政策配合

值得注意的是，上週外匯干預正值日本銀行召開貨幣政策會議期間。
日本央行最終以 8 比 1 決定維持政策利率不變，此前 6 月已將利率上調至 1%，雖創 1995 年以來新高，但仍遠低於美國政策利率水準。
日本央行總裁植田和男在會後表示，未來仍有升息可能，但並未釋出近期將加快升息步調的訊號，使市場對貨幣政策能否配合支撐日元仍存疑慮。
多家機構認為，官方干預短期可望推動日元反彈並引發空頭回補，但若缺乏更強硬的貨幣政策配合，仍難改變日元長期偏弱格局。
根據日本媒體及《金融時報》報導，日本政府與日本央行上週五連續第二天買入日元，美國方面則由紐約聯邦準備銀行代表財政部執行歷史性干預行動，並要求至少兩家大型銀行提供日元相關報價資料。
《彭博》估算，日本當天動用約 8.45 兆日元（約 528 億美元）進場干預，規模可能創下日本史上最大單日匯市干預紀錄。
市場普遍預期，若日元再度快速走弱，美日未來仍可能採取更多聯合干預措施，以穩定匯率走勢。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that the United States participated last week in a foreign‑exchange market intervention led by Japan, helping to support the yen’s price and describing the move as a "friendship signal" to Japan. He said the U.S. backs its allies in stabilising financial markets and expects to reap economic benefits from the arrangement.

Trump told the media on Sunday (the 2nd) while aboard Air Force One that Japan had recently asked for U.S. assistance and that the United States has always supported Japan, maintaining a good bilateral relationship.
He added that, aside from the historic Pearl Harbor episode, Japan has long been an important partner of the United States, so the cooperation carries symbolic significance for bilateral friendship.

When asked what the U.S. would gain from taking part in the intervention, Trump said it would bring "economic benefits" and cited last year’s currency‑swap deal with Argentina as an example, noting that despite domestic criticism at the time, Argentina repaid the funds this year and the U.S. ultimately "earned $25 billion."

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent subsequently voiced public support for the joint action, stressing that the yen had shown excessive and disorderly volatility recently, prompting the U.S. and Japan to intervene together to preserve financial stability.

He pointed out that the Treasury continues close contact with Japan’s Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan, and that a repeat joint intervention is not ruled out if needed, while also backing an expansion of the Fed’s “foreign and international monetary authority repo tool” as a liquidity backstop.

Japan’s Ministry of Finance said the recent intervention aimed to curb abnormal yen swings and that it will keep cooperating with the United States, not ruling out further joint action if necessary, while continuing to use the liquidity tools provided by the Fed and maintaining close communication with Washington.
The rare U.S.–Japan joint effort to support the yen has put markets on alert for possible follow‑up interventions.

Affected by the coordinated U.S.–Japan intervention and a weakening dollar, the yen continued its rise in early Asian trading on Monday (the 3rd), with markets closely watching whether the two countries will step in again.

Earlier, Trump announced a pause in new U.S. military actions against Iran, which sent the dollar lower; the USD/JPY pair fell about 100 points in a single day, sliding to around 156, a drop of more than 1% in one session.

After the joint U.S.–Japan action last week, the yen rebounded sharply. The dollar‑yen rate closed around 157.40 on Friday, its best level since May, whereas before the intervention the yen had neared its lowest since 1986, with USD/JPY approaching 164.

Market participants note that, although daily global FX turnover reaches roughly $9.5 trillion, official intervention may not reverse the yen’s long‑term trend, but it has succeeded in reversing the multi‑month weakness in the short run.
In addition to outright yen purchases, the authorities pressured banks to report exchange‑rate quotes and officials publicly urged market participants, raising the risk of shorting the yen.

Goldman Sachs analysts said that if the yen gives back its recent gains, officials could intervene again in the coming days, as they did in May, arguing that without fundamental improvement, intervention remains an effective tool to buy time and stabilise market expectations.
The yen’s weakness has ripple effects on global finance, and U.S. officials are increasingly concerned about potential impacts on the U.S. Treasury market.
Analysts point out that the yen’s recent pressure stems from higher energy prices, Japan’s expanding fiscal deficit, and a persistently high U.S.–Japan interest‑rate differential.

A weaker yen boosts Japan’s export competitiveness but raises import costs, increasing burdens on firms and households; moreover, volatility in Japan’s financial markets could spill over globally via capital flows, drawing heightened U.S. attention.

Mizuho Bank strategists say the episode matters not only for the intervention itself but also because markets now see excessive yen weakness as a global financial stability issue, not just a Japanese problem.

The market also believes the U.S. backing of Japan’s intervention has another motive: if Japan acted alone, it might have to sell more U.S. Treasuries for dollars, pushing Treasury yields higher and raising U.S. financing costs. Joint action helps ease pressure on Japan to dump large amounts of U.S. debt.

Rebecca Patterson, senior researcher at the Foreign Relations Committee, noted that Japan has been financing interventions by selling portions of its U.S. Treasury holdings, and a larger future asset‑allocation shift could hit the Treasury market harder, so persuading Japan to curb Treasury sales aligns with U.S. interests.

Separately, a Reuters‑released photo showed Bessent’s notes from a Camp David cabinet meeting listing a to‑do item “Buy $5‑10 billion worth of yen,” seen as evidence of active U.S. participation in the intervention.
It is noteworthy that last week’s FX intervention coincided with a Bank of Japan monetary‑policy meeting.
The BOJ ultimately voted 8‑1 to keep policy rates unchanged; it had raised rates to 1% in June, a peak not seen since 1995, but still well below U.S. policy rates.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said after the meeting that further rate hikes remain possible, but he did not signal an accelerated tightening path, leaving doubts about whether monetary policy will dovetail with yen‑support efforts.

Several institutions believe that while official intervention can spark a short‑term yen rebound and trigger short covering, without a tougher monetary stance the yen’s long‑term weakness is unlikely to be altered.

According to Japanese media and the Financial Times, the Japanese government and BOJ bought yen for the second consecutive day on Friday, while the U.S. side was represented by a New York Fed official acting for the Treasury in a historic intervention that required at least two major banks to provide yen‑related quote data.
Bloomberg estimated that Japan deployed about ¥8.45 trillion (≈$52.8 billion) that day, potentially setting a record for the largest single‑day FX intervention in Japanese history.
The market broadly expects that if the yen weakens sharply again, the U.S. and Japan may resort to further joint interventions to stabilise the exchange‑rate trajectory.

items.title: 福斯全球裁10萬人、BMW也砍8千 德國車廠迎最慘寒冬
items.title_en: Volkswagen Cuts 100,000 Jobs, BMW Trims 8,000 – German Automakers Face Their Harshest Winter
paras: 德國汽車產業正迎來百年來最嚴峻的轉折。過去象徵德國製造實力的車廠，如今卻接連宣布大規模裁員，反映在電動化、智慧化浪潮與全球市場競爭加劇下，傳統車廠正面臨前所未有的轉型壓力。其中，福斯集團（Volkswagen）與 BMW 相繼祭出裁員計畫，更成為這場產業變局的代表性事件，也讓外界開始重新審視德國汽車工業的競爭優勢。
率先投下震撼彈的是福斯集團。根據德國媒體報導，福斯正啟動創立百年來規模最大的組織瘦身計畫，全球裁員人數將由原先德國境內 5 萬人，擴大至全球約 10 萬人。
以福斯目前全球約 66.7 萬名員工計算，裁員比例約達 15%；德國本土約 30 萬名員工則有近 17% 面臨影響，顯示此次改革力度空前。
福斯的震撼尚未平息，BMW 也緊接著宣布裁員計畫。德國《商報》指出，BMW 將自今年 10 月起啟動全球人力精簡，預計至明年底裁減約 8,000 名員工，占全球 15 萬名員工約 5.3%。
雖然裁員比例低於福斯，但此次主要鎖定行政管理、研發規劃及部分技術支援部門，而非生產線人員，意味 BMW 希望透過調整管理架構與提升營運效率，以因應產業快速變化帶來的挑戰。
兩家車廠大幅縮減人力的背後，都指向相同原因──電動化與智慧化轉型成本高昂，傳統燃油車市場成長放緩，加上全球競爭日益激烈，使車廠不得不透過削減成本來維持獲利能力。
BMW 近年的財務表現便反映出這股壓力。2025 年營收、稅前獲利及淨利均較前一年下滑，進入 2026 年後情況進一步惡化，第一季營收年減 8.1%，稅前獲利大減 24.6%，淨利更下滑 23.1%，顯示轉型期的獲利壓力持續升高。
其中，中國市場的疲弱更成為 BMW 業績承壓的重要因素。BMW 曾於 2021 年在中國創下近 85 萬輛的銷售高峰，但此後一路下滑，2022 年已出現自 2005 年以來首次衰退，2025 年銷量降至 62.55 萬輛，今年上半年再年減 20.4%。
數據顯示，隨著新能源車與智慧化功能逐漸成為市場主流，中國消費者對傳統豪華品牌的偏好正在改變，也使 BMW 面臨更大競爭壓力。
事實上，福斯與 BMW 並非個案，而是整個德國汽車產業集體調整的縮影。保時捷近期宣布新增裁員 5,000 人，累計裁員規模將達約 9,000 人，占員工總數超過兩成；賓士則持續推動歷來最大規模的人力精簡，目標至 2027 年底累計裁員 3 萬人。
此外，包括 Bosch、Schaeffler、ZF Friedrichshafen 及大陸集團等大型零組件供應商，也相繼提出數千至上萬人的裁員計畫，顯示整條汽車供應鏈都正面臨轉型陣痛。
裁員潮已開始反映在整體德國工業。資料顯示，2025 年德國工業企業共裁員 12.4 萬人，約為前一年的兩倍，其中汽車產業是重災區。德國汽車工業協會更警告，未來幾年可能還有多達 20 萬個工作機會消失。
汽車工業長期是德國經濟的重要支柱，不僅貢獻約 5% 的國內生產毛額（GDP），也占德國工業增加值約兩成。然而，隨著全球汽車產業重心加速轉向電動化與智慧化，德國車廠過去憑藉燃油車技術建立的競爭優勢正受到挑戰。
福斯、BMW 等龍頭車廠接連大裁員，不僅象徵德國汽車產業告別過去高成長、高福利的黃金時代，也凸顯全球汽車產業版圖正進入新一輪重組，昔日的產業霸主正面臨前所未有的考驗。
paras_en: Germany's automotive industry is confronting the toughest turning point in a century. Former symbols of German manufacturing strength are now announcing massive layoffs, reflecting unprecedented transformation pressure on traditional carmakers amid accelerating electrification, digitalisation, and global competition. Volkswagen Group and BMW have each unveiled cutting‑edge layoff plans, becoming emblematic of this industry upheaval and prompting a reassessment of Germany’s automotive competitive edge.

Volkswagen struck first with a shock announcement. German media report that the group is launching the largest organisational downsizing in its 100‑year history, expanding layoffs from an initial 50,000 in Germany to roughly 100,000 worldwide.

With about 667,000 employees globally, the cuts amount to roughly 15% of Volkswagen’s workforce; in Germany, where it employs about 300,000 people, nearly 17% will be affected, underscoring the unprecedented scale of the reform.

The shockwave did not stop there – BMW followed with its own layoff plan. Germany’s Handelsblatt notes that BMW will begin a global headcount reduction in October, aiming to cut about 8,000 jobs by the end of next year, roughly 5.3% of its 150,000‑strong global staff.

Although the proportion is lower than Volkswagen’s, BMW’s cuts target administrative, R&D planning and certain technical support units rather than production line workers, indicating a focus on reshaping management structures and boosting operational efficiency to meet rapid industry changes.

Both manufacturers’ massive workforce reductions point to the same cause – the high cost of electrification and digital transformation, slowing growth in the traditional internal‑combustion market and intensifying global competition, forcing firms to slash costs to preserve profitability.

BMW’s recent financial performance illustrates this pressure. Revenue, pre‑tax profit and net profit all fell in 2025 compared with the prior year, and the situation worsened in 2026: Q1 revenue dropped 8.1% year‑on‑year, pre‑tax profit plunged 24.6%, and net profit fell 23.1%, showing rising profit strain during the transition.

A weak Chinese market has become a key drag on BMW’s results. After peaking at nearly 850,000 units sold in China in 2021, sales have declined steadily; 2022 saw the first downturn since 2005, and 2025 volumes fell to 625,500 units, with a further 20.4% year‑on‑year drop in the first half of this year.
Data show that as new‑energy and smart‑feature vehicles become mainstream, Chinese consumers’ preference for traditional luxury brands is shifting, increasing competitive pressure on BMW.

In fact, Volkswagen and BMW are not isolated cases but reflect a broader adjustment across Germany’s automotive sector. Porsche recently announced an additional 5,000 layoffs, bringing its total cuts to about 9,000 – over 20% of its workforce; Mercedes‑Benz continues its largest‑ever headcount reduction, targeting a cumulative 30,000 cuts by the end of 2027.

Moreover, major parts suppliers such as Bosch, Schaeffler, ZF Friedrichshafen and Continental have each unveiled plans to lay off thousands to tens of thousands of workers, indicating that the entire automotive supply chain is feeling the pain of transformation.

The layoff wave is already evident in Germany’s overall industry. Data show that German industrial firms dismissed 124,000 workers in 2025, roughly double the previous year’s figure, with the automotive sector hit hardest. The German Association of the Automotive Industry warns that up to 200,000 jobs could disappear in the coming years.

The automotive industry has long been a cornerstone of the German economy, contributing about 5% of GDP and accounting for roughly 20% of industrial value‑added. Yet as the global auto focus shifts rapidly toward electrification and digitalisation, the competitive edge German manufacturers built on internal‑combustion technology is being challenged.

The successive large‑scale layoffs at Volkswagen, BMW and peers not only signal the end of the high‑growth, high‑benefit golden era for Germany’s car industry, but also highlight that the global automotive landscape is entering a new round of restructuring, with former industry leaders facing unprecedented tests.

items.title: AI算力狂潮助記憶體進入賣方市場！美銀：三星長協「限跌不限漲」現貨價格Q4前持續反彈
items.title_en: AI Compute Surge Drives Memory into a Seller's Market! BofA: Samsung's Long-Term Agreements "Limit Drops, No Cap on Rises" Keep Spot Prices Rising Through Q4
paras: 根據美銀美林上周六 (8 月 1 日) 發布的記憶體產業調研報告，AI 伺服器需求持續放量，正把 DRAM 與 NAND 價格推入新一輪上行週期，主要大廠定價權顯著回流供應端，其中三星已將 60% 至 70% 銷售納入長期協議 (LTA) 體系，合約條款呈現鮮明「供方友好」特徵，單季降價空間鎖在 5% 以內，漲價則可達 10% 至 20%，甚至不設上限，對美國大型科技客戶更採五年滾動續簽模式。
根據 TrendForce 最新數據，DRAM 上月合約價月增約 10%，季增 30% 至 50%；DRAMeXchange 報價中，16Gb DDR5 現貨價 51 美元、年漲 733%，16Gb DDR4 達 85.2 美元、年漲 896%，1Tb NAND 晶圓 26.4 美元、年漲 415%；64GB DDR5 伺服器模組合約價突破 1480 美元，創歷史新高。
美銀美林預期，在客戶補庫、OEM 新品備貨與產能釋放慢三重拉動下，現貨價格在今年第四季旺季前仍將續彈。
底層驅動來自雲端巨頭的 AI 資本開支洪流。美銀估算，亞馬遜、微軟、Alphabet、Meta、甲骨文五大廠 2026 年合計資本支出約 7300 億美元、年增約 100%，2027 至 2028 年有望破每年 1 兆美元。
記憶體正從「景氣週期品」轉向「AI 基礎設施剛需」，原廠把新增產能優先轉向 HBM 與伺服器 DRAM，通用料供給被動壓縮。
分析師指出，三星以 LTA 鎖量、以不對稱條款鎖利，意味著記憶體產業從「週期波動」走向「價格剛性」，短期風險則在於雲端廠商自由現金流承壓及 2028 年 LTA 重談，但本輪上行由 AI 算力、長協結構、供需偏緊三者疊加，遠未結束。
paras_en: According to a memory‑industry research report released by BofA Merrill Lynch last Saturday (August 1), the continued expansion of AI server demand is pushing DRAM and NAND prices into a new upward cycle, with major manufacturers regaining significant pricing power on the supply side. Samsung, for example, has placed 60% to 70% of its sales under long‑term agreement (LTA) contracts, whose terms are distinctly "supplier‑friendly": quarterly price cuts are capped at under 5%, while price increases can range from 10% to 20% and may even have no upper limit. For large U.S. tech customers, Samsung uses a five‑year rolling renewal model.

TrendForce’s latest data show that last month DRAM contract prices rose about 10% month‑over‑month and 30%‑50% quarter‑over‑quarter. In DRAMeXchange pricing, the spot price for 16‑Gb DDR5 is $51, up 733% year‑over‑year; 16‑Gb DDR4 reached $85.2, up 896% YoY; a 1‑Tb NAND wafer is $26.4, up 415% YoY; and a 64‑GB DDR5 server module contract price broke $1,480, a historic high.

BofA Merrill Lynch expects that, driven by customers restocking inventories, OEMs building new product stock, and a gradual release of capacity, spot prices will continue to bounce back before the peak season in the fourth quarter of this year.

The underlying driver is the flood of AI‑related capital expenditures from cloud giants. BofA estimates that Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle together will spend about $730 billion on capital expenditures in 2026 – roughly a 100% year‑over‑year increase – and that spending could exceed $1 trillion per year in 2027‑2028.

Memory is shifting from a "cyclical commodity" to an "essential AI infrastructure". Original equipment manufacturers are prioritising new capacity for HBM and server DRAM, compressing the supply of commodity memory.

Analysts note that Samsung’s use of LTAs to lock in volume and asymmetric pricing to lock in profit means the memory industry is moving from "cyclical volatility" to "price rigidity". Short‑term risks include pressure on cloud providers’ free cash flow and the renegotiation of LTAs in 2028, but the current upward trend—driven by AI compute demand, long‑term agreement structures, and tight supply‑demand balance—is far from over.

items.title: 川普表態！美日財政部證實 15年來首次聯合托舉日元
items.title_en: Trump Comments! US and Japan Finance Ministries Confirm First Joint Yen Support in 15 Years
paras: 美國總統川普周日（2 日）表示，美國上周參與了推高日元匯率的外匯市場干預行動，稱這體現了美日友誼，有助於全球經濟。
「他們需要一些幫助，我國始終會向日本伸出援手。」川普周日在「空軍一號」上告訴記者。他提及美日良好盟友關係，還說道：「日本一直對我國很好——當然，珍珠港事件除外。」
上周四、周五兩天，日元匯率在 1986 年以來新低位置多次異動暴拉，引發市場廣泛猜測日本政府再度出手干預匯市。
日本央行的數據顯示，當局為支撐日元匯率，上周四可能賣出高達 589.7 億美元，且上周五疑似再次干預市場。
台灣時間周一早間，也就是川普發出上述講話後不久，美日財政部同步官方證實了聯合干預行動。這是兩國 15 年來的首次聯合干預，旨在支撐遭受重創的日元。
日本財務省稱，7 月 31 日財務省用美元購買了日元。日本與美國協調購買了日元，將毫不猶豫展開進一步聯合干預行動。
美國財長貝森特說，財政部與日本財務省、日本央行保持密切溝通，將毫不猶豫進行更多日元聯合干預。
過去 30 年裡，美國和日本聯合干預匯市只發生過兩次。1998 年亞洲金融危機期間，日美曾協同買入日元；2011 年東日本大地震引發日元異常升值後，美國等西方 7 國與日本展開聯合干預。
日本財務省和美國財政部以數十年來前所未有的力道聯手支撐日元匯率，無疑提高了市場放空日元的風險。
日本一直在努力遏制日元持續下跌。日元貶值不僅推高了進口價格，加劇了整體通膨，從而加重了普通家庭的經濟負擔，也拖累了首相高市早苗的支持率。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday (the 2nd) that the United States participated in foreign‑exchange market intervention last week that helped lift the yen’s exchange rate, calling it a demonstration of the U.S.–Japan friendship and beneficial to the global economy.

“They need some help, and our country will always lend a hand to Japan,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday. He referenced the strong U.S.–Japan alliance and added, “Japan has always been good to us—except for Pearl Harbor, of course.”

On Thursday and Friday of last week, the yen surged repeatedly from its lowest level since 1986, sparking widespread market speculation that the Japanese government was intervening in the currency market again.
Data from the Bank of Japan show that authorities may have sold up to $58.97 billion on Thursday to support the yen, and on Friday they are suspected of intervening again.

Early on Monday Taiwan time, shortly after Trump’s remarks, the U.S. and Japanese finance ministries officially confirmed the joint intervention. This is the first coordinated action between the two countries in 15 years, aimed at bolstering the heavily weakened yen.

Japan’s Ministry of Finance said that on July 31 it used dollars to purchase yen. Japan coordinated the purchase with the United States and said it would not hesitate to launch further joint interventions.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen said the Treasury is in close communication with Japan’s Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan and will not hesitate to conduct more joint yen interventions.

In the past 30 years, the United States and Japan have jointly intervened in the FX market only twice: during the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when the two countries bought yen together; and after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, when the United States and six other Western nations coordinated with Japan to curb an abnormal yen appreciation.

The Japanese Ministry of Finance and the U.S. Treasury are joining forces with unprecedented strength in decades to support the yen, clearly raising the risk for market participants who are shorting the currency.

Japan has been working hard to stop the yen’s continued decline. A weaker yen not only pushes up import prices and fuels overall inflation, increasing the economic burden on ordinary families, but also drags down the approval rating of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

items.title: 川普證實美伊週一談判登場！暫緩軍事行動拚重開荷姆茲海峽
items.title_en: Trump Confirms US‑Iran Talks to Begin Monday, Pauses Military Action to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
paras: 美國總統川普證實，美方與伊朗的談判將於週一（3 日）登場，但他拒絕為協議設下最後期限。此前他曾表示，自己已取消原本迫在眉睫的軍事攻擊，希望能儘快達成協議，重新開放荷姆茲海峽，並解決德黑蘭核能力僵局。
根據《路透》報導，川普週六（1 日）深夜在自家社群平台 Truth Social 發文指出，伊朗及其他中東國家要求給予更多時間完成一項協議，該協議將促成荷姆茲海峽「立即、全面且完全」重新開放，並「終結伊朗的核威脅」，但他也強調，德黑蘭必須「迅速達成協議」。
川普結束在新澤西州度過的週末返回華府途中，於週日（2 日）向媒體表示，談判將於週一下午開始，但未透露談判地點，也未說明參與人員。
當被問及是否為伊朗設定達成協議的期限時，川普拒絕回答。
他表示：「我是否更希望達成協議？我不想殺人，因為那樣會死人，很多人會死，我們不想那樣。」
自今年 2 月底與以色列共同對伊朗發動軍事行動以來，川普多次揚言將升高對伊朗的戰事，以爭取更多時間進行談判。然而，迄今談判仍未促成一項全面性的協議。
在雙方連日互相威脅發動新一輪攻擊後，川普如今似乎轉向降溫局勢，成為這場戰爭最新的發展轉折。目前戰火已從波斯灣擴大至紅海，甚至波及埃及地中海沿岸的一處設施。
伊朗在戰爭爆發後大幅封鎖荷姆茲海峽。這條海峽在戰前承載全球約 20% 的原油與液化天然氣運輸，因此封鎖措施推升能源價格，並進一步加劇整體通膨壓力。
川普主張，防止伊朗取得核武是美國的核心目標，因此即使短期內燃料價格上漲也有其正當性。然而，能源成本攀升帶來的經濟壓力，也使他面臨愈來愈大的政治壓力，必須尋求結束這場衝突的方法。
週一早盤交易中，國際油價下跌逾 4%。

伊朗展開外交斡旋

伊朗國營媒體週日報導，伊朗外交部長阿拉格齊（Abbas Araqchi）分別與沙烏地阿拉伯外交部長費瑟 · 本 · 法爾漢 · 阿紹德（Prince Faisal bin Farhan）及巴基斯坦陸軍參謀長穆尼爾（Asim Munir）通話，討論外交斡旋工作。
伊朗官方通訊社《IRNA》此前報導，援引阿拉格齊說法指出，德黑蘭與阿曼就荷姆茲海峽相關議題的談判已進入最後階段。
不過，伊朗外交部發言人巴蓋伊（Esmaeil Baghaei）表示，談判重點是就一條新的航運路線達成協議，並強調此事「與荷姆茲海峽是否重新開放或關閉無關，那是另一項獨立議題。」
上個月，伊朗曾公開拒絕由阿曼提出、並獲波灣國家支持的一項管理荷姆茲海峽的方案。知情人士此前向《路透》表示，該方案內容包括向使用海峽的船舶收取自願性費用。
另一方面，以色列能源部長、同時也是該國總理納坦雅胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）安全內閣成員的 Eli Cohen 表示，以色列與美國就區域局勢的所有發展都保持密切的安全與情報合作。
不過他也警告：「無論是否達成協議，也不論有任何外部承諾，只要伊朗試圖重啟核計畫或推進彈道飛彈產業，我們都會採取行動，並發動打擊。」
川普與納坦雅胡上週二在華府會晤。一名以色列官員表示，雙方已探討遏制伊朗核計畫的所有可能途徑，包括外交談判、經濟施壓以及軍事手段。伊朗則一再否認尋求發展核武。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that negotiations between the United States and Iran will take place on Monday (the 3rd), but he refused to set a deadline for any agreement. He previously said he had called off an imminent military strike in hopes of reaching a deal quickly, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resolving the stalemate over Tehran’s nuclear capability.

According to Reuters, Trump posted late on Saturday (the 1st) on his own social‑media platform Truth Social that Iran and other Middle‑East countries are asking for more time to complete an agreement that would lead to the "immediate, comprehensive and complete" reopening of the Hormuz Strait and "end Iran’s nuclear threat," but he stressed that Tehran must "reach an agreement quickly."
Trump, returning to Washington after a weekend in New Jersey, told the media on Sunday (the 2nd) that the talks would start on Monday afternoon, without revealing the venue or the participants.
When asked whether he had set a deadline for Iran to reach a deal, Trump declined to answer.
He said, "Do I want to reach a deal more? I don’t want to kill people, because that would cause deaths, many people would die, and we don’t want that."

Since the joint U.S.–Israeli military action against Iran at the end of February, Trump has repeatedly threatened to intensify the war against Iran to buy more time for negotiations. Yet, to date, the talks have not produced a comprehensive agreement.

After days of mutual threats to launch a new round of attacks, Trump now appears to be cooling the situation, marking the latest turning point in the war. The fighting has spread from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea and even affected a facility on Egypt’s Mediterranean coast.

Iran dramatically blocked the Strait of Hormuz after the war began. The strait carried about 20% of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the conflict, so the blockade pushed energy prices higher and added to overall inflation pressure.

Trump argues that preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons is the core U.S. objective, so short‑term fuel price spikes are justified. However, the economic strain from rising energy costs is increasing political pressure on him to find a way to end the conflict.
In early Monday trading, international oil prices fell more than 4%.
Iran launches diplomatic outreach

Iranian state media reported on Sunday that Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi held calls with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir to discuss diplomatic mediation efforts.
Iran’s official news agency IRNA previously quoted Araqchi as saying that talks with Oman on Hormuz‑related issues have entered their final stage.

However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the negotiations focus on reaching an agreement on a new shipping route and stressed that this issue "is unrelated to whether the Hormuz Strait is reopened or closed; that is a separate matter."

Last month Iran publicly rejected a proposal put forward by Oman and backed by Gulf states to manage the Strait of Hormuz, which, according to sources cited by Reuters, would have involved voluntary fees for vessels using the strait.

On the other side, Israeli Energy Minister and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s security cabinet member Eli Cohen said Israel and the United States maintain close security and intelligence cooperation on all regional developments.

He warned, "Whether or not an agreement is reached, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to restart its nuclear program or advance its ballistic‑missile industry, we will act and strike."

Trump met Netanyahu in Washington last Tuesday. An Israeli official said the two discussed every possible way to curb Iran’s nuclear program, including diplomatic talks, economic pressure and military options. Iran continues to deny it is seeking nuclear weapons.

items.title: 美財長貝森特手寫紙條曝光！美國罕見出手救日元  背後是美債危機考量？
items.title_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent’s Handwritten Note Exposed! Rare U.S. Intervention to Support the Yen – Driven by Concerns Over a U.S. Debt Crisis?
paras: 日元兌美元上週四（30 日）、五（31 日）連續劇烈震盪，一度觸及 1986 年以來最低水準，市場原本已預期日本政府將再度進場干預匯市。然而真正引發全球關注的，卻是華府這回竟也罕見出手相挺。
多家外媒引述知情人士報導，美國政府週五指示紐約聯邦準備銀行執行「拋歐元、買日元」操作，協助穩住搖搖欲墜的日元匯價。
這項消息的最直接佐證，來自美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）一張被媒體鏡頭捕捉到的手寫紙條。
當地時間週五，川普在馬里蘭州戴維營度假地主持內閣會議並進行現場直播，貝森特一如往常坐在川普對面。
在鏡頭環伺之下，貝森特毫不避諱地在筆記本上寫下:「待辦事項：買進日元，50 億至 100 億美元。」這張紙條隨即被拍下並迅速在全球流傳開來。

三十年來罕見合作，分析憂心殃及美債

回顧過去三十年，美日兩國聯手干預匯市的紀錄僅有兩次：

一次是 1998 年亞洲金融風暴期間，雙方協同買進日元；
另一次則發生在 2011 年東日本大地震後，日元一度異常飆升，美國與其他七國隨即與日本展開聯合干預行動。


值得玩味的是，貝森特過去正是外匯市場的老手，曾在 2012 年主導索羅斯基金放空日元，短短三個月內大賺逾十億美元。
如今卻反過來親自下場「馳援」日元，外界解讀此舉恐怕別有考量，即避免日本金融情勢失控，進而波及美國公債市場。
畢竟受美伊軍事緊張及聯準會新任主席華許（Kevin Warsh）信任危機影響，美國長天期公債殖利率上週才剛創下次貸風暴以來新高。
事實上，今年 1 月日本首相高市早苗財政政策一度引爆「日債風暴」，花旗集團當時便警告，該波動盪恐觸發規模高達 1300 億美元的美債拋售潮。
據悉，美方官員私下已向日方表達憂慮，擔心高市早苗的激進財政路線可能重演英國前首相特拉斯（Liz Truss）當年引爆市場崩跌的覆轍。

日本外匯存底加速消耗，成效仍待觀察

儘管日本當局近期已大手筆動用外匯存底救市，成效卻相當有限。
市場估算，光是上週四單日，日本政府與央行的干預規模就達到 6 兆至 7 兆日元，加上 4 月底至 5 月底期間投入的 11.7 兆日元（約合 743 億美元），累計干預金額已攀升至 18 兆日元（約 1143 億美元），一舉超越 2024 年創下的 15.3 兆日元歷史紀錄。
美國財政部先前公布的國際資本流動報告也顯示，日本 5 月確實拋售了 667.5 億美元美國公債，金額與其外匯干預規模大致吻合。
然而，那波干預效果僅維持約一個月，日元至 6 月初便已貶回干預前的低點。
日本財務省週六凌晨也透過社群媒體發文表示，在適當情況下不排除動用聯準會的「外國暨國際貨幣當局常設回購機制」(FIMA Repo Facility)，透過以美國公債作為擔保品，取得臨時性美元流動性支援。
外界解讀，貝森特似乎也意識到，單靠匯市砸錢恐怕無法根治日元貶值問題。他週五特別在社群平台上發文，表示期待 8 月底於 G20 會議期間與日本央行總裁植田和男「再度會面」。
巧合的是，植田和男上週五在宣布維持利率不變後，亦於會後記者會上罕見鬆口，暗示未來不排除「加快升息步伐」的可能性。
paras_en: The yen versus the dollar saw violent swings on Thursday (the 30th) and Friday (the 31st) last week, briefly hitting its lowest level since 1986. Markets had expected the Japanese government to step in again to intervene in the FX market. However, the story that captured global attention was that Washington this time also made a rare move to support the currency.

Several foreign media outlets, citing insiders, reported that the U.S. government instructed the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Friday to carry out a “sell euros, buy yen” operation to help steady the wobbling yen exchange rate.
The most direct evidence of this came from a handwritten note by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that was captured on camera by the media.

On Friday local time, President Trump hosted a cabinet meeting and live broadcast from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Maryland, with Bessent seated opposite him as usual. Under the watchful eye of the cameras, Bessent unabashedly wrote in his notebook: “To‑do: buy yen, $5‑10 billion.” The note was immediately photographed and quickly spread worldwide.
A collaboration not seen in thirty years raises worries about U.S. debt

Looking back over the past three decades, there have been only two instances of joint U.S.–Japan intervention in the FX market: one during the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when both sides coordinated to buy yen; and another after the 2011 Great East Japan earthquake, when the yen surged sharply and the U.S. and seven other countries joined Japan in a coordinated intervention.

It is noteworthy that Bessent himself was once a veteran of the FX market, having led a Soros fund short‑sell of the yen in 2012, netting more than $1 billion in profit within three months. Now he is personally “rushing to the rescue” of the yen, which analysts interpret as a move motivated by concerns that a loss of control over Japan’s financial situation could spill over into the U.S. Treasury market.

Indeed, amid heightened U.S.–Iran tensions and a credibility crisis for new Fed chair Kevin Warsh, long‑term U.S. Treasury yields only last week reached their highest level since the last debt‑crisis‑induced credit crunch.

In fact, in January this year Japanese Prime Minister Naïve Takashi’s fiscal policy sparked a “Japanese‑bond storm,” prompting Citigroup to warn that the turbulence could trigger up to $130 billion of U.S. Treasury sell‑offs.
U.S. officials have reportedly privately expressed concern to Japan that Takashi’s aggressive fiscal stance could repeat the market collapse caused by former UK Prime Minister Liz Truss.
Japan’s foreign‑exchange reserves are being depleted rapidly, and the impact of recent interventions remains uncertain
Although Japanese authorities have recently deployed massive foreign‑exchange reserves to prop up the market, the effect has been limited.

Market estimates put last Thursday’s single‑day intervention by the Japanese government and central bank at ¥6‑7 trillion, and combined with the ¥11.7 trillion (about $74.3 billion) deployed from the end of April to the end of May, total intervention has risen to ¥18 trillion (about $114.3 billion), surpassing the record ¥15.3 trillion set in 2024.
The U.S. Treasury’s International Capital Flows report also shows that Japan sold $66.75 billion of U.S. Treasuries in May, an amount roughly matching the scale of its FX intervention.
However, that wave of intervention only lasted about a month; by early June the yen had already slipped back to its pre‑intervention lows.

In the early hours of Saturday, Japan’s Ministry of Finance posted on social media that, if appropriate, it would not rule out using the Federal Reserve’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Permanent Repo Facility (FIMA Repo) to obtain temporary dollar liquidity by pledging U.S. Treasuries as collateral.

Observers note that Bessent seems to realize that simply throwing money at the FX market cannot cure the yen’s depreciation. On Friday he posted on social media that he looks forward to meeting Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda again at the G20 summit at the end of August.

Coincidentally, after announcing that rates would remain unchanged last Friday, Ueda also made a rare comment at the post‑meeting press conference, hinting that a faster pace of rate hikes could not be ruled out in the future.

items.title: 日元空頭瑟瑟發抖！川普高調背書美日聯手託市、貝森特筆記泄露天機
items.title_en: Yen Short Sellers Tremble! Trump Boasts US‑Japan Joint Market Support, Bessent Note Leaks the Plan
paras: 美國總統川普證實，美國上週參與日本主導的外匯市場干預行動，協助支撐日元匯價，並形容此舉是對日本釋出的「友誼訊號」。他表示，美方支持盟友穩定金融市場，同時也預期能從相關安排中取得經濟利益。
川普週日（2 日）在搭乘空軍一號時向媒體表示，日本近期希望獲得美方協助，而美國一向支持日本，兩國維持良好關係。
他也提到，除了歷史上的珍珠港事件外，日本長期以來都是美國的重要夥伴，因此此次合作具有象徵雙邊友誼的意義。
對於美國參與干預能獲得哪些回報，川普僅表示將帶來「經濟利益」，並拿去年與阿根廷簽署的貨幣互換安排作為例子，稱儘管當時受到美國國內批評，但阿根廷今年已償還相關資金，美方最終「賺取了 250 億美元」。
美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）隨後也公開表態支持這項協同行動，強調近期日元出現過度且無序波動，美日因此共同採取外匯干預措施，以維護金融穩定。
他指出，美國財政部持續與日本財務省及日本銀行保持密切聯繫，必要時不排除再次聯手進場，並支持擴大聯準會的「外國與國際貨幣當局回購工具」，作為市場流動性的後盾。
日本財務省則表示，近期干預目的在於遏止日元異常波動，未來將持續與美國合作，必要時不排除進一步採取聯合行動，同時持續運用聯準會提供的流動性工具，並與美方保持密切溝通。

美日罕見聯手支撐日元 市場戒備後續干預

受美日協調干預及美元走弱影響，日元週一（3 日）亞洲盤初延續升勢，市場則密切觀察兩國是否將再次聯手進場。
此前，川普宣布暫緩對伊朗採取新的軍事行動，帶動美元回落，美元兌日元一度快速下跌約 100 點，跌至 156 附近，單日跌幅逾 1%。
日本與美國上週共同出手後，日元已明顯反彈。美元兌日元上週五收在 157.40 左右，創 5 月以來最佳表現；而在干預前，日元一度逼近 1986 年以來最低水準，美元兌日元曾接近 164。
市場人士指出，雖然全球每日外匯交易規模高達約 9.5 兆美元，官方干預未必足以扭轉日元長期走勢，但短線已成功逆轉日元連續數月的弱勢。
除了直接買入日元外，美日當局也透過要求銀行回報匯率報價，以及官員公開喊話等方式向市場施壓，提高放空日元的風險。
高盛分析師指出，若日元再度回吐近期漲幅，不排除官方未來數日再次進場干預，如同今年 5 月的情況。他們認為，在基本面尚未改善前，干預仍是官方爭取時間、穩定市場預期的有效工具。

日元疲弱牽動全球金融 美方憂衝擊美債市場

分析人士指出，日元近年持續承壓，主要受到能源價格上漲、日本財政赤字擴大，以及美日利差維持高檔等因素影響。
日元貶值雖有助日本出口競爭力，但也推升進口成本，增加企業與民眾負擔；另一方面，日本金融市場波動也可能透過全球資本流動影響其他市場，美國對此愈來愈關注。
瑞穗銀行策略師表示，這次事件的重要性不只在於干預本身，更代表市場開始相信，日元過度疲弱已不再只是日本的問題，而是可能牽動全球金融穩定。
市場也認為，美國支持日本干預還有另一層考量。若日本單獨支撐日元，可能需要出售更多美國公債換取美元資金，進一步推升美債殖利率並增加美國融資成本，因此美方選擇共同出手，有助降低日本大規模拋售美債的壓力。
外交關係委員會資深研究員 Rebecca Patterson 指出，日本已透過出售部分美債籌措干預資金，若未來出現更大規模資產配置調整，可能對美債市場帶來更大衝擊，因此說服日本避免持續出售美債，符合美國利益。
另一方面，《路透》日前公布的一張照片也引發市場關注。照片顯示，貝森特在戴維營內閣會議的筆記中，於待辦事項欄位寫下「買入 50 億至 100 億美元日元」，被視為美國積極參與干預的重要跡象。

日本央行按兵不動 市場仍關注政策配合

值得注意的是，上週外匯干預正值日本銀行召開貨幣政策會議期間。
日本央行最終以 8 比 1 決定維持政策利率不變，此前 6 月已將利率上調至 1%，雖創 1995 年以來新高，但仍遠低於美國政策利率水準。
日本央行總裁植田和男在會後表示，未來仍有升息可能，但並未釋出近期將加快升息步調的訊號，使市場對貨幣政策能否配合支撐日元仍存疑慮。
多家機構認為，官方干預短期可望推動日元反彈並引發空頭回補，但若缺乏更強硬的貨幣政策配合，仍難改變日元長期偏弱格局。
根據日本媒體及《金融時報》報導，日本政府與日本央行上週五連續第二天買入日元，美國方面則由紐約聯邦準備銀行代表財政部執行歷史性干預行動，並要求至少兩家大型銀行提供日元相關報價資料。
《彭博》估算，日本當天動用約 8.45 兆日元（約 528 億美元）進場干預，規模可能創下日本史上最大單日匯市干預紀錄。
市場普遍預期，若日元再度快速走弱，美日未來仍可能採取更多聯合干預措施，以穩定匯率走勢。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that the United States participated last week in a foreign‑exchange market intervention led by Japan, helping to support the yen’s price and describing the move as a "friendship signal" to Japan. He said the U.S. backs its allies in stabilising financial markets and expects to reap economic benefits from the arrangement.

Trump told the media on Sunday (the 2nd) while aboard Air Force One that Japan had recently asked for U.S. assistance and that the United States has always supported Japan, maintaining a good bilateral relationship.
He added that, aside from the historic Pearl Harbor episode, Japan has long been an important partner of the United States, so the cooperation carries symbolic significance for bilateral friendship.

When asked what the U.S. would gain from taking part in the intervention, Trump said it would bring "economic benefits" and cited last year’s currency‑swap deal with Argentina as an example, noting that despite domestic criticism at the time, Argentina repaid the funds this year and the U.S. ultimately "earned $25 billion."

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent subsequently voiced public support for the joint action, stressing that the yen had shown excessive and disorderly volatility recently, prompting the U.S. and Japan to intervene together to preserve financial stability.

He pointed out that the Treasury continues close contact with Japan’s Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan, and that a repeat joint intervention is not ruled out if needed, while also backing an expansion of the Fed’s “foreign and international monetary authority repo tool” as a liquidity backstop.

Japan’s Ministry of Finance said the recent intervention aimed to curb abnormal yen swings and that it will keep cooperating with the United States, not ruling out further joint action if necessary, while continuing to use the liquidity tools provided by the Fed and maintaining close communication with Washington.
The rare U.S.–Japan joint effort to support the yen has put markets on alert for possible follow‑up interventions.

Affected by the coordinated U.S.–Japan intervention and a weakening dollar, the yen continued its rise in early Asian trading on Monday (the 3rd), with markets closely watching whether the two countries will step in again.

Earlier, Trump announced a pause in new U.S. military actions against Iran, which sent the dollar lower; the USD/JPY pair fell about 100 points in a single day, sliding to around 156, a drop of more than 1% in one session.

After the joint U.S.–Japan action last week, the yen rebounded sharply. The dollar‑yen rate closed around 157.40 on Friday, its best level since May, whereas before the intervention the yen had neared its lowest since 1986, with USD/JPY approaching 164.

Market participants note that, although daily global FX turnover reaches roughly $9.5 trillion, official intervention may not reverse the yen’s long‑term trend, but it has succeeded in reversing the multi‑month weakness in the short run.
In addition to outright yen purchases, the authorities pressured banks to report exchange‑rate quotes and officials publicly urged market participants, raising the risk of shorting the yen.

Goldman Sachs analysts said that if the yen gives back its recent gains, officials could intervene again in the coming days, as they did in May, arguing that without fundamental improvement, intervention remains an effective tool to buy time and stabilise market expectations.
The yen’s weakness has ripple effects on global finance, and U.S. officials are increasingly concerned about potential impacts on the U.S. Treasury market.
Analysts point out that the yen’s recent pressure stems from higher energy prices, Japan’s expanding fiscal deficit, and a persistently high U.S.–Japan interest‑rate differential.

A weaker yen boosts Japan’s export competitiveness but raises import costs, increasing burdens on firms and households; moreover, volatility in Japan’s financial markets could spill over globally via capital flows, drawing heightened U.S. attention.

Mizuho Bank strategists say the episode matters not only for the intervention itself but also because markets now see excessive yen weakness as a global financial stability issue, not just a Japanese problem.

The market also believes the U.S. backing of Japan’s intervention has another motive: if Japan acted alone, it might have to sell more U.S. Treasuries for dollars, pushing Treasury yields higher and raising U.S. financing costs. Joint action helps ease pressure on Japan to dump large amounts of U.S. debt.

Rebecca Patterson, senior researcher at the Foreign Relations Committee, noted that Japan has been financing interventions by selling portions of its U.S. Treasury holdings, and a larger future asset‑allocation shift could hit the Treasury market harder, so persuading Japan to curb Treasury sales aligns with U.S. interests.

Separately, a Reuters‑released photo showed Bessent’s notes from a Camp David cabinet meeting listing a to‑do item “Buy $5‑10 billion worth of yen,” seen as evidence of active U.S. participation in the intervention.
It is noteworthy that last week’s FX intervention coincided with a Bank of Japan monetary‑policy meeting.
The BOJ ultimately voted 8‑1 to keep policy rates unchanged; it had raised rates to 1% in June, a peak not seen since 1995, but still well below U.S. policy rates.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said after the meeting that further rate hikes remain possible, but he did not signal an accelerated tightening path, leaving doubts about whether monetary policy will dovetail with yen‑support efforts.

Several institutions believe that while official intervention can spark a short‑term yen rebound and trigger short covering, without a tougher monetary stance the yen’s long‑term weakness is unlikely to be altered.

According to Japanese media and the Financial Times, the Japanese government and BOJ bought yen for the second consecutive day on Friday, while the U.S. side was represented by a New York Fed official acting for the Treasury in a historic intervention that required at least two major banks to provide yen‑related quote data.
Bloomberg estimated that Japan deployed about ¥8.45 trillion (≈$52.8 billion) that day, potentially setting a record for the largest single‑day FX intervention in Japanese history.
The market broadly expects that if the yen weakens sharply again, the U.S. and Japan may resort to further joint interventions to stabilise the exchange‑rate trajectory.

items.title: 川普表態！美日財政部證實 15年來首次聯合托舉日元
items.title_en: Trump Comments! US and Japan Finance Ministries Confirm First Joint Yen Support in 15 Years
paras: 美國總統川普周日（2 日）表示，美國上周參與了推高日元匯率的外匯市場干預行動，稱這體現了美日友誼，有助於全球經濟。
「他們需要一些幫助，我國始終會向日本伸出援手。」川普周日在「空軍一號」上告訴記者。他提及美日良好盟友關係，還說道：「日本一直對我國很好——當然，珍珠港事件除外。」
上周四、周五兩天，日元匯率在 1986 年以來新低位置多次異動暴拉，引發市場廣泛猜測日本政府再度出手干預匯市。
日本央行的數據顯示，當局為支撐日元匯率，上周四可能賣出高達 589.7 億美元，且上周五疑似再次干預市場。
台灣時間周一早間，也就是川普發出上述講話後不久，美日財政部同步官方證實了聯合干預行動。這是兩國 15 年來的首次聯合干預，旨在支撐遭受重創的日元。
日本財務省稱，7 月 31 日財務省用美元購買了日元。日本與美國協調購買了日元，將毫不猶豫展開進一步聯合干預行動。
美國財長貝森特說，財政部與日本財務省、日本央行保持密切溝通，將毫不猶豫進行更多日元聯合干預。
過去 30 年裡，美國和日本聯合干預匯市只發生過兩次。1998 年亞洲金融危機期間，日美曾協同買入日元；2011 年東日本大地震引發日元異常升值後，美國等西方 7 國與日本展開聯合干預。
日本財務省和美國財政部以數十年來前所未有的力道聯手支撐日元匯率，無疑提高了市場放空日元的風險。
日本一直在努力遏制日元持續下跌。日元貶值不僅推高了進口價格，加劇了整體通膨，從而加重了普通家庭的經濟負擔，也拖累了首相高市早苗的支持率。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday (the 2nd) that the United States participated in foreign‑exchange market intervention last week that helped lift the yen’s exchange rate, calling it a demonstration of the U.S.–Japan friendship and beneficial to the global economy.

“They need some help, and our country will always lend a hand to Japan,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday. He referenced the strong U.S.–Japan alliance and added, “Japan has always been good to us—except for Pearl Harbor, of course.”

On Thursday and Friday of last week, the yen surged repeatedly from its lowest level since 1986, sparking widespread market speculation that the Japanese government was intervening in the currency market again.
Data from the Bank of Japan show that authorities may have sold up to $58.97 billion on Thursday to support the yen, and on Friday they are suspected of intervening again.

Early on Monday Taiwan time, shortly after Trump’s remarks, the U.S. and Japanese finance ministries officially confirmed the joint intervention. This is the first coordinated action between the two countries in 15 years, aimed at bolstering the heavily weakened yen.

Japan’s Ministry of Finance said that on July 31 it used dollars to purchase yen. Japan coordinated the purchase with the United States and said it would not hesitate to launch further joint interventions.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen said the Treasury is in close communication with Japan’s Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan and will not hesitate to conduct more joint yen interventions.

In the past 30 years, the United States and Japan have jointly intervened in the FX market only twice: during the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when the two countries bought yen together; and after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, when the United States and six other Western nations coordinated with Japan to curb an abnormal yen appreciation.

The Japanese Ministry of Finance and the U.S. Treasury are joining forces with unprecedented strength in decades to support the yen, clearly raising the risk for market participants who are shorting the currency.

Japan has been working hard to stop the yen’s continued decline. A weaker yen not only pushes up import prices and fuels overall inflation, increasing the economic burden on ordinary families, but also drags down the approval rating of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

paras: 上週，美國、日本、韓國三方罕見聯手，實施近 30 年來最大規模的協調外匯干預行動，不只壓制日元、韓元貶值，更被市場解讀為美國穩住盟友金融市場、防止亞洲資產波動倒灌華爾街的「聯合救市」。
東京當局上周四 (7 月 30 日) 單日動用約 8.45 兆日元 (約 528 億美元) 拋售美元、買入日元，規模居史上前列，同日南韓外匯當局也罕見入市拋美元，韓元單日升值 2% 至 9 個月高點。
隔天，美國財政部透過紐約聯準銀行委託高盛、摩根士丹利「賣歐元、買日元」，為 1998 年來美國首次直接參與日元干預。三方出手後，美元兌日元自 162 上方摔落至 157—159 區間，日元脫離 40 年低點。
美國下場方式極具技術性。正式交易前，紐約聯準銀行連兩日先做「匯率檢查」，上周四查美元兌日元、上周五查歐元兌日元，只問價不成交，釋放信號。
美銀外匯策略師 Alex Cohen 指出，「匯率檢查」介於口頭喊話與真金白銀之間，是美國財政部今年新用的壓力工具，選歐元通道而非美元通道，意在挺日元同時不增美元供給、護住美元指數。
南韓副財長 Moon Ji-sung 證實與美日密切協調，日本財務省副大臣三村淳直言，美方支持「已超越單純道義聲援」。背景是日韓市場同步承壓，KOSDAQ 摔到 2022 年 10 月以來低點，科技股去槓桿未完，日元韓元續弱恐引發亞洲資產連鎖重估。
華爾街更關注「為什麼是現在」。美銀策略師 Hartnett 將此次行動稱為 AI 時代「價格維持操作」(PKO)，因日韓皆為美國半導體與 AI 供應鏈核心，三星、SK 海力士、東京電子牽動全球算力擴張，若本幣崩貶推高日債收益率、逼出套利交易平倉，火會燒到美債與美股。美
因此，美國要降三大類風險：防日元急貶炸日債利率、防金融壓力擴散亞洲、防無序資本流衝擊美債。今年以來，半導體 ETF 吸金約 530 億美元，費半指數短線回檔，但 AI 資本開支邏輯未破，華府不願盟友資產在槓桿尾聲被空頭收割。
不過干預≠趨勢反轉。匯率檢查能嚇退投機，但若日美利差未收、韓股去槓桿未淨，日元韓元仍可能被重新測試。
市場共識是：這輪協調先把「無序貶值」按住，替 8 月南韓監管落地、日本央行 (BOJ) 下月利率評估買時間，真正定價權回歸，仍看半導體獲利、企業回購與全球 AI 開支。
近 30 年首見的美方直接下場，訊號意義已大過金額本身，華府把日韓匯率與資產穩定，正式列為本土金融防線的一環。
paras_en: Last week, the United States, Japan and South Korea unusually joined forces to carry out the largest coordinated foreign‑exchange intervention in nearly three decades. The operation not only curbed the yen and won’s depreciation but was also read by the market as a joint "rescue" aimed at stabilising allied financial markets and preventing Asian asset volatility from spilling over onto Wall Street.

On Thursday, July 30, Tokyo authorities sold roughly ¥8.45 trillion (about $52.8 billion) of dollars and bought yen in a single‑day operation, a scale that ranks among the biggest in history. On the same day, South Korean foreign‑exchange officials also entered the market to sell dollars, pushing the won up 2% to a nine‑month high.

The next day, the US Treasury, via the New York Federal Reserve Bank and through Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, sold euros and bought yen – marking the first time since 1998 that the United States directly participated in yen intervention. After the three‑way action, the dollar‑yen rate fell from above 162 to the 157‑159 band, pulling the yen out of a 40‑year low.

The US’s exit strategy was highly technical. Before any trades were executed, the New York Fed conducted two days of “rate checks”: on Thursday it probed the dollar‑yen pair, and on Friday the euro‑yen pair, asking for quotes without actually transacting, thereby sending a signal to the market.

Bank of America foreign‑exchange strategist Alex Cohen explained that a “rate check” sits between a verbal warning and a real trade, and is a new pressure tool the Treasury has adopted this year. By targeting the euro‑yen channel rather than the dollar‑yen channel, the US aimed to support the yen without increasing dollar supply and to protect the dollar index.

South Korean Deputy Finance Minister Moon Ji‑sung confirmed close coordination with the US and Japan, while Japanese Ministry of Finance Vice‑Minister Mitsumura Jun‑nao said US support had "gone beyond a purely moral endorsement." The backdrop was simultaneous pressure on both markets: the KOSDAQ had fallen to its lowest level since October 2022, tech‑stock deleveraging was still underway, and continued weakness in the yen and won risked triggering a chain‑reaction revaluation of Asian assets.

Wall Street was more focused on "why now." Bank of America strategist Hartnett labelled the move a price‑maintenance operation (PKO) for the AI era, noting that both Japan and South Korea are core to the US semiconductor and AI supply chain – companies like Samsung, SK Hynix and Tokyo Electron drive global compute expansion. A collapse of their currencies could push Japanese bond yields higher and force arbitrage unwindings, which would then spread to US Treasuries and equities.

Thus, the US aims to reduce three major risks: preventing a sharp yen drop that would spike Japanese bond yields, containing financial stress from spilling across Asia, and averting disorderly capital flows that could hit US bonds. Since the start of the year, semiconductor ETFs have attracted about $53 billion, the semiconductor index has pulled back in the short term, but the logic of AI‑driven capital spending remains intact, and Washington does not want its allies’ assets to be harvested by short‑sellers at the end of the leverage cycle.

However, intervention does not equal a trend reversal. Rate checks can scare off speculators, but if the US‑Japan interest‑rate differential remains unaddressed and Korean equity deleveraging is not resolved, the yen and won could still be tested again.

The market consensus is that this round of coordination first contains "disorderly depreciation," buying time for South Korean regulators to implement August measures and for the Bank of Japan to assess rates next month. True pricing power will return based on semiconductor earnings, corporate buybacks and global AI spending.

The US’s direct involvement – a first in 30 years – carries a signal that outweighs the monetary amount itself. Washington is now treating the stability of Japanese and Korean exchange rates and assets as an integral part of its domestic financial defence line.

paras: 日本政府可能再度大規模進場支撐日元，根據日本央行帳戶數據與市場機構估算，日本當局週四 (30 日) 疑似買進日元、拋售美元，規模約達 8.45 兆日元 (約 528 億美元)。日媒隨後報導，日本週五可能連續第二天干預匯市；同一時間，美國財政部與紐約聯準銀行也傳出採取準備行動，使市場更加相信美日正在協調遏止日元貶勢。
